headline: Smoother frame caps, controller switching and fixes for Quartu land in Development
summary: Development gains more precise frame timing and controller selection by first press, addressing gamepads overlooked behind USB-C docks (#146, #149). Ratchet & Clank fixes cover the PAL flight to Quartu, a ship-landing crash with extra enemies, and missing Suck Cannon gauge graphics with the HUD at the edges (#151, #147, #150). Larger modded maps gain expanded memory and authoring support (#148). Enhanced rendering gains a native preparation pipeline, compressed lighting probes and water material improvements, but its author calls it very work in progress (#154).
highlights: #152 closes #39, #48, #66, #127, #135 and #141 with Quartu drowning, texture-pack, Going Commando PAL extraction, mod-asset, remapping and NTSC lighting preparation fixes. A new lighting-region limit failure is reported in #159.
Menu text with anti-aliasing on Intel Arc and menu flicker without it on Adreno get fixes. Collision queries can now be checked against the original game code (#145, #157).

Flights show the destination name and shorten the stop afterward. Black fills reach the screen edges, level preparation runs at lower priority, and Linux launcher lists fade in correctly (#156, #155, #144, #153).
Ordinary sessions retain the original 32 MiB memory arena. A follow-up restores their original actor-class capacity after the modded-map expansion (#148, #158).

Proposed mod install links, dependency handling and auto-update remain unmerged. Their author has not tested Windows, macOS or Android (#161). The decompilation import and faster Vulkan tests are also only proposals (#160, #163).
The enhanced-rendering work accounts for most of the day’s added lines (#154). Repository references now use openrac-mods (#162).
